summary: Aldrich Butte's standing three-story cab dates to 1960, replacing a 1959 cab that vandals burned; sources name three different staffing agencies.

facts.design: three-story ODF flat-roof live-in cab, 14x14 ft with catwalk (1960 replacement); the 1934 site had an L-4 cab

staffing.status: staffed per the NHLR (ODF) and, in summer, per firelookout.com (undated); the Aug 2023 forest notice says BLM mans it, so the agency is disputed

access.note: The Aug 2023 Malheur NF notice says public parking is available at the lookouts and visitors are welcome in daylight hours, and asks visitors to respect staff after hours. No source says whether the cab can be entered.

events.note: Site first used as a lookout in 1934; firelookout.com says it was developed with an L-4 cab
Three-story frame live-in ODF cab built in 1959
1959 cab burned by vandals the same year
Present lookout built in 1960 as an identical replacement to the same standard; NHLR calls it a three-story ODF flat-roof design with 14x14 ft cab and catwalk
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register on January 8, 2003
Aug 15, 2023 Malheur NF notice lists Aldrich Lookout as an ODF lookout manned by the Bureau of Land Management

corrections.proposed: three-story ODF flat-roof live-in cab, 14x14 ft with catwalk (1960 replacement); the 1934 site had an L-4 cab
corrections.why: L-4 is the 1934 cab per firelookout.com. The standing 1960 cab is the three-story ODF design described by the NHLR.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR says the Oregon Department of Forestry built and staffs the tower. Undated firelookout.com says the Ochoco National Forest staffs it each summer. The Aug 2023 Malheur NF notice says it is manned by the Bureau of Land Management. The story reports all three; the 2023 notice is the newest source found.
Sources give 1934 for first lookout use, 1959 for the burned cab and 1960 for the standing cab. The record uses 1960 for the present structure, as the brief did.
The NHLR gives 6,912 ft (2,107 m) and firelookout.com gives 6988 ft. Elevation is not a supported facts key here, so the story does not use either figure.

sources.title: Malheur National Forest staffs fire lookouts

notes_for_editor: Brief record: design L-4 describes the 1934 cab, not the standing 1960 cab; correction proposed. Staffing is disputed across three sources (NHLR: ODF; firelookout.com undated: Ochoco NF; Aug 2023 Malheur NF notice: BLM). Access is provisional: the 2023 notice is the only source on visitor access and says nothing about entering the cab. Search results also included a different Aldrich Butte in Washington, near North Bonneville; it was not used. No photos were added: the NHLR and firelookout.com photo credits have no licence or URL in what was read.
